name: Evelyn van Kelle
bio:
I’ve always been curious. Especially about people and what happens when you throw a bunch of very different humans into a room and expect them to build something together. Spoiler: it’s never just about the technology. My background in social sciences means I look at software development and organizations through a sociotechnical lens: how human behavior, social dynamics, and group decision-making shape what actually gets built (and whether it works).

I thrive on questions more than answers, experiments more than certainties, and the learning that comes from exploring complexity rather than simplifying it away. Curiosity drives my work, whether I’m exploring cognitive biases in decision-making, helping teams and leadership navigate conflict, or figuring out how organizations can change without burning people out. 

Along the way, I realized my childhood dream of writing a book, co-authoring Collaborative Software Design - how to facilitate domain modeling decisions. I also love sharing what I learn and (think I) know at international conferences, meetups, and podcasts. And if you ever want to dive into (or rant about) how humans + tech collide, I’m your person.

You can find my blogs and gigs here: https://evelynvankelle.com/
